summary.text: Alan Gordon, a Republican who co-leads The Healing Church, which uses cannabis in religious services, and is not a lawyer, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Attorney General of Rhode Island to Kimberly Ahern.

He holds a self-designed bachelor’s degree and an LL.B. from the University of Buckingham in England, ran for attorney general in 2018 as the Compassion Party nominee, and describes himself as a longtime cannabis activist.

paragraphs.text: Gordon earned a self-designed Bachelor of Arts at Penn State in 1992, focused on the legal and public-policy questions surrounding cannabis reform, and an honors LL.B. from the University of Buckingham in England in 2012, according to his campaign biography.
The same biography says he passed the England and Wales bar examinations, and that he chose not to seek admission to the Rhode Island Bar.
He is not a lawyer, NBC 10 reported.

Since 2014, Gordon says, he has provided private ecclesiastical legal guidance to several Christian church organizations, including service as legal advisor to a bishop of the Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church from 2014 to 2022 and to the matriarch of the Hebrew Catholic Church.
He and Anne Armstrong, a one-time gubernatorial candidate, lead the Healing Church; in 2015 they sought to smoke cannabis as part of a religious ceremony at Roger Williams Park.
In 2018 Gordon was the Compassion Party's nominee for attorney general.

In the 2026 campaign, Gordon opposed Rhode Island's bans on assault weapons and large-capacity magazines, telling NBC 10 that courts would have to look at them as restrictions on the right to bear arms.
He was anti-abortion but told the station he would not try to change the state law codifying abortion rights.
His campaign site listed defending constitutional rights, protecting vulnerable people, confronting public corruption and applying one standard of justice among its priorities.
He received 33.4% of the vote to Kimberly Ahern's 66.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
